definitions.explanation: Physically or spatially right in front of someone. Describes something visible and immediately present.
Temporally very near, about to happen. Used when an event, deadline, or situation is approaching and nearly upon one.

examples.japanese: {目前|もくぜん}に{海|うみ}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: The sea spread out right before my eyes.

examples.japanese: {危険|きけん}が{目前|もくぜん}に{迫|せま}っている。
examples.english: Danger is closing in right before us.

examples.japanese: {目前|もくぜん}で{事故|じこ}が{起|お}きて、{体|からだ}が{凍|こお}りついた。
examples.english: An accident happened right before my eyes and I froze.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}が{目前|もくぜん}に{迫|せま}っている。
{締|し}め{切|き}りを{目前|もくぜん}に{控|ひか}えている。
examples.english: The deadline is close at hand.

examples.japanese: {卒業|そつぎょう}を{目前|もくぜん}にして、{将来|しょうらい}について{真剣|しんけん}に{考|かんが}え{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: With graduation imminent, I started to think seriously about the future.

notes:
USAGE:
Used adverbially with the particle に or で. The phrase {目前|もくぜん}に{迫|せま}る (to be closing in / to be imminent) is extremely common in both senses. The pattern ～を{目前|もくぜん}にして (with ~ imminent, on the eve of ~) is also frequently used.

WRITING:
{目|もく} means "eye" and {前|ぜん} means "before" or "in front of." The compound literally means "before the eyes."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目前|もくぜん}に{迫|せま}る: to be imminent / to approach
- ～を{目前|もくぜん}にして: with ~ imminent, on the eve of ~
- {目前|もくぜん}に{控|ひか}える: to be close at hand
